summary: Retest of the 4 critical permission issues from iteration_16. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration17_permission_fixes.py (21 tests) covering super_admin bypass, reminders gating (reminders.view / reminders.send), email-logs owner-only, and passport token/rotate gating (customers.view / customers.edit) — all 21 PASSED. Replayed the full iteration_16 matrix (36 tests) — all PASSED, 0 leaks, no previously-403 endpoint unlocked. Owner end-to-end flow (customer → vehicle → job card → part → invoice → mark-paid) passed. Frontend smoke: warehouse@test.com logs in, lands on /inventory, sidebar shows exactly nav-inventory + nav-my-profile, /suppliers URL bounced back to /inventory, and ZERO 401/403/500 network responses were captured.
critical_code_review_comments: has_permission() now grants a blanket bypass to role=='super_admin' on every tenant data endpoint. This is intentional per the impersonation design, but it means a platform admin can read/write any tenant's customers, invoices and email logs directly without an impersonation token and without an audit trail. Consider logging super_admin data access.

reminders.register() and email_logs.register() keep a get_current_user fallback when the guard arg is not wired (`_guard = require_owner if require_owner else get_current_user`). This fails open; if a future refactor drops the arg the endpoints silently become unguarded. Prefer raising at import/registration time.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral TEST_* staff users (reminders.view, reminders.view+send, inventory.view+edit, customers.view, customers.view+edit) and TEST_ customer/vehicle/inventory/invoice records — all deleted in fixture teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Permission matrix is fully green as of iteration 17. Regression suites to reuse: tests/test_iteration16_permissions.py (matrix + owner e2e flow) and tests/test_iteration17_permission_fixes.py (4 fixes). Fixed a flaky skip in iter16's passport test (it only looked at the first customer for a vehicle; now iterates). Endpoints still on plain get_current_user (not scope-guarded) and worth auditing next: /api/settings, /api/rdw/lookup.
rca_of_the_issue: iter16 failures were: (1) has_permission() bypassed only role=='owner' so super_admin got 403 on data endpoints; (2)(3) reminders.py and email_logs.py registered their endpoints with get_current_user because the guard dependencies were never passed into register(); (4) passport token/rotate used get_current_user instead of require_permission. All four are now fixed and verified via direct HTTP calls against the public preview URL.
